findings.summary: Travel returns to above its pre-pandemic level in FY2021 and is twice that level by FY2023, while the firm's own records show it working from home into late 2021 and holding its client sessions by call or video.
findings.evidence: Travel line in the financial summaries: FY2019 $121,320 (d:0041), FY2020 $35,190 (d:0050), FY2021 $139,900 (d:0053), FY2022 $183,200 (d:0055), FY2023 $244,210 (d:0063). FY2023 is 8.1% of revenue, the highest share in the firm's history. The same corpus says: d:0043 (June 2020) 'The whole firm is working from home for now'; d:0051 (August 2021) a building card that may lapse 'after a stretch at home'; d:0052 (November 2021) 'Several of us are back in the office part of the week'. The only working sessions whose medium is stated were 'held by conference call' (d:0037, 2019) or 'held by video conference' (d:0047, d:0049). For desk-based actuarial work, a 2021 travel spend 15% above 2019 does not match the era: the 2020 shock lasts exactly one year and then the trend resumes as if nothing happened.

findings.summary: The Martinez LLC retiree medical valuation is priced at $118,500. That is the largest fee in the book and nearly four times the pension valuation, for a client small enough that its General Manager gathers the data himself.
findings.evidence: Ledger fees, all fixed: E-2020-001 retiree medical valuation for ASC 715 reporting $118,500 (stated in d:0044 and d:0048); E-2016-001 pension funding valuation, including a takeover model build and an assumption review, $30,500 (d:0002); E-2017-001 reserve adequacy opinion for an insurer $78,000; E-2019-001 experience study $65,000. On the client's size: d:0045 'Jason Wagner, General Manager at [the client], will coordinate the data for the company himself'; d:0047 retiree contributions are set each year and the company 'follows no formula'. A benefits actuary would expect one retiree medical plan valuation for a client like this to be priced at or below the firm's pension funding valuation, not at 3.9 times it and above the insurer reserve opinion.

findings.summary: Office & Facilities is identical to the dollar for four consecutive years, twice. The occupancy line reads as a step function, not as a rent bill that also carries escalations, utilities and repairs.
findings.evidence: Office & Facilities is $147,000 in each of FY2015, FY2016, FY2017 and FY2018 (d:0001, d:0013, d:0026, d:0029), $163,800 in each of FY2019 through FY2022 (d:0041, d:0050, d:0053, d:0055), then $186,000 in FY2023 (d:0063). Every other expense line changes every year. FY2015 also matches the later full years exactly, although foundation.json records the firm moving into its current office on 2015-10-15, partway through that year.
